assessment_summary:
Step 1: Valid. A k-chromatic graph contains a k-critical subgraph H.
Step 2: Valid. The minimum degree of a k-critical graph is at least k-1.
Step 3: Valid. By definition of k-critical, H-vk is (k-1)-colorable.
Step 4: Valid. Adding vk as its own partition Vk creates a valid partition of H.
Step 5: Valid. Orienting edges from lower to higher index partitions is a well-defined operation.
Step 6: Valid. The orientation is acyclic because edges only go from lower to higher indexed independent sets.
Step 7: Flawed. A greedy backward path construction can get stuck; an arbitrarily chosen neighbor of vk in Vk-1 is not guaranteed to have any neighbors in Vk-2.
Step 8: Flawed. Arbitrarily orienting additional edges of G can easily create directed paths with more than k vertices, violating the exactly k vertices requirement.
